about.title: Sebastopol Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Sebastopol sits in Sonoma County, where agriculture, construction, retail, and delivery work all carry their own hazards. If you were hurt on the job here, California generally routes your claim through workers' compensation regardless of who was at fault. But comp doesn't cover everything, and it doesn't apply to everyone who contributed to your injury. If a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver played a role — say, in a work-related collision near Rt 12 or Bodega Avenue — you may have a separate injury claim against that third party, on top of any comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we're a free service that connects you with an independent attorney familiar with both workers' comp and third-party claims in Sonoma County, so you understand which path applies to your situation and what deadlines matter.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Workplace Injury

items.title: Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but it doesn't shield a negligent third party like a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker. An attorney can tell you whether a separate claim applies to your case.

items.title: Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and any third-party claim carries a 2-year deadline. Missing either window can limit your options, so it helps to get guidance early.

items.title: Retaliation Is Against the Law
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from punishing workers for reporting an injury or filing a claim. An attorney can help you understand your protections if you're worried about your job.

items.question: I was hurt on a delivery route near Rt 116. Do I file workers' comp or a regular injury claim?
items.answer: Likely both could apply. Workers' comp typically covers your medical care and lost wages regardless of fault, but if another driver caused the crash, you may also have a separate claim against that driver. An attorney can walk through the details of your Sebastopol case and explain which claims fit.

items.question: What if my employer says I waited too long to report my injury?
items.answer: California generally expects injuries reported within 30 days, but exceptions and disputes come up often, especially with injuries that develop gradually. Talking to an attorney sooner rather than later gives you the best chance to preserve your options.

items.question: Can I be fired for filing a workers' comp claim in Sebastopol?
items.answer: No, retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an independent attorney can advise you on next steps specific to your situation.
